title: Linear-size circuits for stable 0,1 < 2 sorting?
review_status: Accepted by accompanying independent AI-assisted mathematical audit; unrefereed
unconditional_status: The general linear-size question remains unresolved: Omega(n) lower and O(n log n) upper bounds.
conditional_status: Theta(n log n) only under the undirected k-pairs conjecture in the precise form used by AFKL.
accepted_components: Canonical bit-level rank-parity O(n log n) circuit and O(log^2 n) depth.
Correct O(n)-overhead shift restrictions, including the half-garbage power-of-two promise.
Conditional matching Omega(n log n) via AFKL Theorem 2 under its stated undirected k-pairs conjecture.
Regan balanced reduction with required output mask.
Specific three-wire counterexample to Regan Theorem 1 stability assertion; independent survival of comparator lower bound.
not_accepted_as_claims: An unconditional superlinear general-circuit lower bound.
A proof or refutation of the network-coding conjecture.
Novelty or priority over all literature.
remaining_gap: No O(n) general Boolean circuit or unconditional superlinear general Boolean-circuit lower bound is established. The conditional lower bound cannot be promoted to unconditional. Finite tests cannot close this gap.
prior_conditional_barrier_credit: Asharov–Lin–Shi already discusses the conditional stable-compaction barrier; no novelty or priority is claimed.
